content: Turn classification from a path polyline has a settled convention. ArcGIS 'turn category evaluator': classify each two-edge transition into four general turn types - Left Turn, Right Turn, Straight Ahead, Reverse - using turn azimuth; default azimuth range for right/left is 30 to 150 degrees (right clockwise, left counterclockwise), so straight is a rotation less than the minimum azimuth and reverse is a U-turn or a rotation beyond the maximum azimuth. Creating explicit turn features for every turn is 'often infeasible because of the quantity of turns', which is why generalised azimuth classification is used. HERE and Mapbox expose the same idea as a 'step' list with a maneuver type plus a location. GIS StackExchange has parallel implementations of turn-from-polyline. This directly supports the project's left/right/straight/u-turn classifier over consecutive path bearings.
